destinations.name: Bangalore Palace
destinations.description: A Tudor-revival palace begun in the 1860s and bought by Maharaja Chamaraja Wodeyar in 1878, standing in the middle of 450 acres of grounds. Its wooden carvings, fortified towers, cornices and fortified interiors draw heavily on English Gothic and Scottish castle styles.
destinations.hours: Approx. 10:00-17:30, may vary on public holidays
destinations.facilities: Guided tours, gardens, parking, audio guide, restrooms
destinations.accessibility: Ground floor largely step-free; upper floors by stairs

destinations.name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
destinations.description: A 240-acre botanical garden begun by Hyder Ali in 1760 and completed by Tipu Sultan, home to one of India's largest collections of tropical plants and a glass house modelled on London's Crystal Palace. A granite outcrop inside the garden is estimated at around 3,000 million years old.
destinations.fee_note: Free entry; small fee on some special days
destinations.season: Any season; flower shows in January and August
destinations.facilities: Glass house, lake, walking paths, restrooms, drinking water, parking
destinations.accessibility: Level paths in most areas; some slopes

destinations.name: Cubbon Park
destinations.description: A 300-acre green lung in the centre of Bengaluru, laid out in 1870, holding the red Attara Kacheri building, the State Central Library and a children's toy train. It is a popular early-morning walking and birdwatching spot.
destinations.facilities: Walking tracks, toy train, library, restrooms, drinking water
destinations.accessibility: Wide level paths; largely wheelchair friendly

destinations.name: ISKCON Sri Radha Krishna Temple, Rajajinagar
destinations.description: A large hilltop temple complex on Hare Krishna Hill, consecrated in 1997, with an ornate gold-plated gopuram and a hall seating over a thousand people. The complex also houses a restaurant and a cultural centre.
destinations.facilities: Prasada counter, restaurant, lift, cloakroom, parking

destinations.name: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace
destinations.description: A 1791 teak-and-plaster summer palace of Tipu Sultan, with carved wooden pillars, ornate balconies and painted walls, now protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. It sits inside a small walled garden near the City Market.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (ASI monument; indicative demo price shown)
destinations.hours: Approx. 09:00-17:00, closed on some ASI holidays
destinations.facilities: Information boards, restrooms nearby, parking on the road
destinations.accessibility: Ground level; small step at the entrance

destinations.name: National Gallery of Modern Art, Bengaluru
destinations.description: Housed in the restored Manikyavelu Mansion on Palace Road, this gallery shows modern and contemporary Indian art across two floors and a sculpture garden. Exhibitions rotate through the year.

destinations.name: Bull Temple (Dodda Basavana Gudi)
destinations.description: A 16th-century Basavanagudi temple built by Kempe Gowda I, sheltering a large monolithic Nandi bull carved from a single rock. The groundnut fair, Kadalekai Parishe, is held on the road outside every year.
destinations.season: Any season; November for the groundnut fair
destinations.accessibility: Steps at the entrance; crowded during festivals

destinations.name: Devanahalli Fort
destinations.description: A 16th-century stone fort built by Mallabairegowda, later rebuilt in the 18th century, and the birthplace of Tipu Sultan. The old town inside its walls holds several temples and the Venugopalaswamy temple.

destinations.name: Ghati Subramanya Temple
destinations.description: A hill-based temple near Doddaballapura dedicated to Subramanya, famous for its combined shrine of Subramanya and Narasimha facing one another. The temple is crowded during the annual serpent festival.

destinations.name: Makalidurga Fort and Hill
destinations.description: A hill fort at roughly 1,100 m reached by a two-hour trek past the Makalidurga railway station, with a hilltop temple and wide views over the plains. The trek route is popular with weekend hikers.
destinations.facilities: Village at the base; no facilities on the hill
destinations.accessibility: Steep rocky trail; not suitable for limited mobility

destinations.name: Shivagange
destinations.description: A pilgrimage hill of about 1,360 m in Nelamangala taluk, climbed by stone steps to a temple, a perennial spring and an old Nandi monolith. The hill is also known for its rock formations and views.
destinations.facilities: Shops at the base, restrooms, parking
destinations.accessibility: Several hundred steps; no vehicle access to the top

destinations.name: Mysore Palace
destinations.description: The seat of the Wodeyar dynasty and one of India's most visited monuments, with a 145-ft domed tower, a Durbar Hall, and an interior of carved rosewood, stained glass and painted murals. The building is illuminated with close to a lakh bulbs every Sunday evening and during Dasara.
destinations.hours: Approx. 10:00-17:30; palace lit on Sunday evenings
destinations.season: October to February; Dasara in Sep-Oct
destinations.facilities: Audio guide, cloakroom, restrooms, parking, illumination on Sundays
destinations.accessibility: Ground floor accessible; upper floors by stairs

destinations.name: Chamundeshwari Temple, Chamundi Hills
destinations.description: A temple to Chamundeshwari on a hill about 13 km from the city, reached by road or by a flight of 1,000 steps. The hill also carries a large Nandi monolith and views across Mysuru.
destinations.facilities: Prasada counter, restrooms, parking, bus service to the hill
destinations.accessibility: Steps at the shrine; road access to the entrance

destinations.name: St. Philomena's Church
destinations.description: A neo-Gothic church built in the 1930s with twin 175-ft spires, stained glass windows and a crypt holding a relic of St. Philomena. It is one of the tallest churches in India.
destinations.hours: Approx. 05:00-18:00; closed to visitors during Mass

destinations.name: Mysore Zoo (Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens)
destinations.description: One of India's oldest zoos, opened in 1892, with over 160 species including giraffes, elephants, tigers and gorillas across landscaped grounds. The zoo runs conservation breeding programmes and is best visited early in the day.
destinations.facilities: Animal enclosures, restrooms, drinking water, canteen, parking, wheelchairs on request
destinations.accessibility: Paved walkways; wheelchair and stroller friendly

destinations.name: Jaganmohan Palace Art Gallery
destinations.description: A former royal residence turned art gallery holding works by Raja Ravi Varma and other Indian artists, along with royal memorabilia. The building dates from the 1860s and was used as the temporary palace after a fire at the main palace.
destinations.accessibility: Steps at the entrance; no lift

destinations.name: Karanji Lake Nature Park
destinations.description: A lake and nature park maintained by the Mysore Zoo, with a walk-through aviary, a butterfly park and a boating jetty. Migratory birds use the lake in winter.
destinations.facilities: Aviary, butterfly park, boating, restrooms, parking

destinations.name: Abbey Falls
destinations.description: A waterfall on a tributary of the Kaveri about 9 km from Madikeri, dropping roughly 70 ft between coffee plantations and spice gardens. Access is by a short path and a suspension bridge.
destinations.season: June to September for volume; October to February for access
destinations.accessibility: Path with steps; slippery in rain

destinations.name: Raja's Seat
destinations.description: A garden and viewpoint on a hillock in Madikeri where the Kodagu rajas are said to have watched sunsets, with terraced lawns, fountains and views into the valley. The garden is a short walk from the town centre.

destinations.name: Talakaveri
destinations.description: The source of the Kaveri on the Brahmagiri hill in Bhagamandala taluk, with a temple tank fed by a spring and a shrine to the goddess Kaveriamma. The site is a major pilgrimage stop during Tula Sankramana.
destinations.season: October to March; Tula Sankramana in October
destinations.accessibility: Steps around the tank; hill road access

destinations.name: Namdroling Monastery, Bylakuppe
destinations.description: One of the largest Tibetan Buddhist monasteries in India, in the Tibetan settlement at Bylakuppe, with a teaching hall and three large gilded Buddha statues. The monastery is an active centre of the Nyingma tradition.
destinations.facilities: Prayer halls, guest house, shops, parking
destinations.accessibility: Ground level; ramps in main areas

destinations.name: Dubare Elephant Camp
destinations.description: A forest camp on the Kaveri near Kushalnagar where trained elephants are bathed and fed, run with the forest department. Visitors cross the river by boat to reach the camp.
destinations.facilities: Boat crossing, elephant interaction, restrooms, parking
destinations.accessibility: River crossing by boat; uneven ground

destinations.name: Mandalpatti Viewpoint
destinations.description: A high grassland ridge above Madikeri reached by a rough jeep track, looking over coffee estates and the Pushpagiri range. Jeeps are hired locally from Madikeri.
destinations.fee_note: Free entry; local jeep hire charged separately
destinations.hours: Daylight hours; early morning for clear views

destinations.name: Panambur Beach
destinations.description: A broad beach beside Mangaluru port known for its sunsets and for hosting the annual kite festival. Water sports and food stalls operate in season.
destinations.hours: Open all day; lifeguards in daylight hours
destinations.facilities: Food stalls, water sports, restrooms, parking
destinations.accessibility: Sandy access; some facilities on raised decks

destinations.name: Kadri Manjunath Temple
destinations.description: An ancient temple in Mangaluru with a bronze Lokeshwara idol dated to around the 10th century, and a spring-fed tank beside the shrine. The temple is an important centre of the Nath tradition in coastal Karnataka.

destinations.name: Sultan Battery
destinations.description: A small watchtower built in the 1780s by Tipu Sultan to guard the Gurupura river entrance, overlooking the old port. It is a short drive from Tannirbhavi beach.

destinations.name: Kudroli Gokarnath Temple
destinations.description: A large temple in central Mangaluru rebuilt in the early 20th century, with an ornate gopuram and shrines to Gokarnath and other deities. Its Dasara celebrations draw large crowds.

destinations.name: Pilikula Nisargadhama
destinations.description: A large nature park near Moodushedde with a biological park, a lake with boating, a heritage village and a science centre on one campus. It is run by the district administration as an educational and recreation site.
destinations.facilities: Zoo, boating, heritage village, science centre, restaurant, restrooms, parking

destinations.name: Tannirbhavi Beach
destinations.description: A quieter beach north of Mangaluru across the Gurupura river, reached by road or by ferry, with casuarina groves and a tree park. It is a common evening spot for local families.
destinations.facilities: Tree park, food stalls, restrooms, parking
destinations.accessibility: Sandy access; ferry is not accessible for wheelchairs

destinations.name: Murudeshwar Temple and Statue
destinations.description: A Shiva temple on the coast at Murudeshwar, dominated by a 123-ft statue of Shiva and a 20-storey gopuram with a lift to the viewing gallery. The site sits on a headland between the sea and the Western Ghats.
destinations.fee_note: Free entry; lift to the gallery ticketed
destinations.facilities: Lift to gopuram, prasada counter, restrooms, parking
destinations.accessibility: Lift available; steps at the shrine

destinations.name: Mahabaleshwara Temple, Gokarna
destinations.description: One of the most important Shiva temples on the west coast, holding the Atmalinga, and the focus of Gokarna's religious life. The temple tank and the main street around it are part of the town's character.
destinations.facilities: Temple tank, restrooms, parking outside the car street
destinations.accessibility: Steps at the entrance; car street is pedestrian

destinations.name: Om Beach, Gokarna
destinations.description: A twin-crescent beach shaped like the Om symbol, north of Gokarna town, with shacks, rocks and a headland walk to Kudle beach. It is the best known of Gokarna's beaches.
destinations.facilities: Beach shacks, guest houses, parking at the access point
destinations.accessibility: Steps and a slope down to the sand

destinations.name: Yana Caves
destinations.description: Two towering black limestone monoliths, Bhairaveshwara and Mohini Shikhara, rising out of the forest in Kumta taluk, with a cave shrine at the base. A trek of about 2 km from the road leads to the site.
destinations.facilities: Small shops at the trailhead; no facilities at the caves
destinations.accessibility: Forest trail with steps; not accessible for wheelchairs

destinations.name: Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary
destinations.description: A sanctuary on the Kali river known for river rafting, coracle rides, hornbill sightings and forest camping. The river stretch at Dandeli is one of the state's main white-water rafting sites in season.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (forest entry; indicative demo price shown)
destinations.facilities: Rafting operators, jungle lodges, guides, restrooms
destinations.accessibility: Forest trails; rafting not suitable for children under 14

destinations.name: Mirjan Fort
destinations.description: A laterite fort near Kumta with high walls, bastions, wells and a stepped tank, associated with the Pepper Queen Chennabhairadevi. The fort is largely in ruins and is a protected monument.
destinations.facilities: None on site; small shops nearby
destinations.accessibility: Rough ground with steps and uneven walls

destinations.name: Unchalli Falls (Lushington Falls)
destinations.description: A 381-ft waterfall on the Aghanashini river near Siddapur, reached by a steep forest path of steps. The falls are at their strongest soon after the monsoon.
destinations.facilities: Viewing deck at the end of the path
destinations.accessibility: Long flight of steps; not suitable for limited mobility

destinations.name: Sri Krishna Matha
destinations.description: The 13th-century matha founded by Madhvacharya, where Krishna is worshipped through a nine-holed window, and the centre of Udupi's famous cuisine and Paryaya festival. The temple complex includes the Chandramouleshwara and Anantheshwara shrines.
destinations.season: Any season; Paryaya every two years in January

destinations.name: Malpe Beach
destinations.description: A wide beach at the mouth of the Malpe river with a fishing harbour, water sports and ferries to St. Mary's Island. The beach is a short drive from Udupi town.
destinations.hours: Open all day; ferry service in daylight
destinations.facilities: Water sports, food stalls, ferry jetty, restrooms, parking
destinations.accessibility: Sandy access; ferry boarding requires steps

destinations.name: St. Mary's Island
destinations.description: A small island of columnar basalt formations off Malpe, reached by a 20-minute ferry, with clear water and a lighthouse view. The rock columns are a notified national geological monument.
destinations.facilities: Ferry from Malpe, small stalls on the island
destinations.accessibility: Ferry boarding by steps; no facilities for limited mobility

destinations.name: Kaup Beach and Lighthouse
destinations.description: A rocky beach south of Udupi with a 27-m lighthouse built in 1901 that can be climbed for views along the coast. The rocks and the sunset make it a popular evening stop.
destinations.accessibility: Rocky ground; lighthouse by spiral stairs

destinations.name: Kodi Bengre Beach
destinations.description: A narrow spit of land between the Suvarna river and the Arabian Sea, north of Udupi, known for its estuary views and quiet fishing village. Boats and local ferries cross the river nearby.

destinations.name: Anantheshwara Temple, Udupi
destinations.description: One of the oldest temples in Udupi, adjoining the Krishna Matha, with a stone idol of Anantheshwara and a history going back over a thousand years. It forms part of the temple cluster around Car Street.

destinations.name: Jog Falls
destinations.description: India's second-highest plunge waterfall, where the Sharavathi river drops about 830 ft in four separate falls, Raja, Rani, Rocket and Roarer, in Sagara taluk. A long flight of steps leads from the viewpoint to the base.
destinations.season: July to January for water; December for the steps
destinations.accessibility: Steps to the base; viewpoints are at road level

destinations.name: Agumbe
destinations.description: A hill village in the Western Ghats known as the Cherrapunji of the south for its heavy rainfall, with sunset points, rainforest trails and a research station for king cobras. Agumbe was the setting for the television adaptation of Malgudi Days.
destinations.hours: Daylight hours; leeches in the monsoon

destinations.name: Kodachadri
destinations.description: A 1,343-m peak in the Western Ghats inside the Mookambika reserve, with a temple at the summit and grasslands below. It is usually climbed from Kollur or reached by jeep from Nagodi.
destinations.fee_note: Free entry; jeep hire charged locally
destinations.facilities: Jeep operators, forest checkpost, temple at the top
destinations.accessibility: Trek of several hours; jeep track is rough

destinations.name: Sakrebailu Elephant Camp
destinations.description: An elephant training camp on the Tunga river near Shivamogga, where visitors can watch the morning bathing and feeding of camp elephants. Entry is through the forest department.
destinations.fee_note: Free entry; forest department rules apply

destinations.name: Shivappa Nayaka Palace
destinations.description: A 17th-century palace in Shivamogga city built in the Nayaka style, now a museum of sculpture and local history under the state archaeology department. Its carved wooden pillars and stone base are the main features.
destinations.hours: Approx. 09:00-17:00, closed on some public holidays
destinations.accessibility: Ground floor; a few steps at the entrance

destinations.name: Gudavi Bird Sanctuary
destinations.description: A small wetland sanctuary near Sorab where thousands of migratory birds, including herons, ibis and cormorants, nest on trees in and around the lake between June and November. It is best visited from a boat or the watchtower.

destinations.name: Mullayanagiri
destinations.description: At about 1,930 m, the highest peak in Karnataka, with a temple at the summit and a road that climbs most of the way from Chikkamagaluru. The last stretch is a flight of steps.
destinations.hours: Daylight hours; early morning for clear views
destinations.facilities: Small stalls, parking below the summit
destinations.accessibility: Road to near the top, then steps

destinations.name: Baba Budangiri
destinations.description: A range and shrine associated with the Sufi saint Baba Budan, credited with bringing coffee to India, set in shola grassland above 1,800 m. A rough road connects it to Mullayanagiri.
destinations.accessibility: Rough road; steps at the shrine

destinations.name: Kemmangundi (Kemmannugundi)
destinations.description: A hill station at about 1,434 m once used as the summer retreat of the Mysore kings, with rose gardens, viewpoints and the Z Point trail. The Karnataka horticulture department runs a guest house here.
destinations.fee_note: Free entry; garden and viewpoints free
destinations.accessibility: Garden paths; Z Point is a steep walk

destinations.name: Hebbe Falls
destinations.description: A two-tier waterfall near Kemmangundi reached by a jeep track and then a walk through coffee estates, dropping in two stages into a pool. Access is controlled by local jeep operators.
destinations.fee_note: Jeep and entry ticketed (indicative demo price shown)
destinations.facilities: Jeep operators at Kemmangundi, small stalls
destinations.accessibility: Jeep track plus a rough walk; not accessible

destinations.name: Kudremukh National Park
destinations.description: A large national park of shola forest and grassland around the Kudremukh peak, with trekking routes permitted in limited numbers by the forest department. The park is part of a UNESCO World Heritage tentative list area in the Western Ghats.
destinations.fee_note: Trek permit ticketed (indicative demo price shown)
destinations.hours: Trek permits issued for morning starts; closed in parts of the monsoon
destinations.facilities: Forest permits, guides, base camp at Mullodi

destinations.name: Sringeri Sharada Peetham
destinations.description: One of the four mathas established by Adi Shankaracharya, on the banks of the Tunga, with the Sharadamba temple and the Vidyashankara temple. The matha runs a Sanskrit college and a large kitchen for pilgrims.
destinations.facilities: Guest houses, dining hall, restrooms, parking
destinations.accessibility: Steps at the temple; some ramps

destinations.name: Hirekolale Lake
destinations.description: A small lake about 10 km from Chikkamagaluru town with a walking path and views of the Mullayanagiri range. It is a common sunset stop on the way to the hill stations.
destinations.accessibility: Paved path around part of the lake

destinations.name: Belgaum Fort
destinations.description: A large fort of pre-Muslim origins rebuilt by the Rattas and later by the Adil Shahis, with stone walls, bastions and two entrances. Inside are the Kamal Basadi and Jal Mandir Jain temples and a mosque.

destinations.name: Kamal Basadi and Jal Mandir
destinations.description: Two Jain temples inside Belgaum Fort, the Kamal Basadi named for its lotus-shaped ceiling and the Jal Mandir standing in a tank. Both are notable for their carved pillars and Neminatha idols.
destinations.accessibility: Steps; the Jal Mandir is reached by a walkway

destinations.name: Gokak Falls
destinations.description: A waterfall on the Ghataprabha river about 6 km from Gokak town, dropping around 170 ft over sandstone, with a hanging bridge and a 19th-century mill nearby. The falls are close to the town and easy to reach by road.
destinations.accessibility: Path with steps; bridge is narrow

destinations.name: Godachinmalki Falls
destinations.description: A two-step waterfall on the Markandeya river near Gokak, reached by a short descent from the road. The upper fall drops about 25 m into a rocky pool.
destinations.hours: Daylight hours; best soon after the monsoon

destinations.name: Kittur Fort
destinations.description: The ruined fort of Rani Chennamma of Kittur, who fought the British in 1824, with laterite walls, a palace site and a museum. The fort is a state-protected monument.
destinations.accessibility: Rough ground; not suitable for wheelchairs

destinations.name: Naviluteertha (Navilatheertha)
destinations.description: A rock-cut cave site near Belagavi with a large sculpted Nandi and a stepped tank, associated with the Ratta period. It is a quiet protected monument a short drive from the city.

destinations.name: Ballari Fort
destinations.description: A hill fort with two separate citadels, built and rebuilt across the Vijayanagara, Bijapur and British periods, with granaries, temples and a durbar hall inside. It is a protected monument overlooking the town.
destinations.facilities: None on site; town facilities nearby
destinations.accessibility: Steep paths and steps; not accessible

destinations.name: Daroji Sloth Bear Sanctuary
destinations.description: Asia's first sanctuary dedicated to sloth bears, spread over about 82 sq km of rocky scrub near Kamalapur. Bears are usually seen from a watchtower in the early morning or evening.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (forest entry; indicative demo price shown)

destinations.name: Kumaraswamy Temple, Sandur
destinations.description: A hilltop temple near Sandur reached by a long flight of steps, with views over the Sandur hills and the surrounding iron-ore landscape. The temple is busy during its annual festival.
destinations.facilities: Shops at the base, restrooms, parking

destinations.name: Tungabhadra Dam and Garden, Hosapete
destinations.description: A large dam across the Tungabhadra with terraced gardens, a musical fountain and a lighthouse-style viewpoint, about 6 km from Hosapete. It is the main water source for the Ballari and Koppal regions.
destinations.fee_note: Free entry; garden and fountain ticketed on some days
destinations.accessibility: Paved paths and steps; some areas sloped

destinations.name: Gol Gumbaz
destinations.description: The mausoleum of Muhammad Adil Shah, built from 1626, with one of the largest domes in the world and a whispering gallery where a sound carries across the hall. It is the defining monument of Bijapur.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (ASI monument; indicative demo price shown)
destinations.accessibility: Ground level accessible; gallery by stairs

destinations.name: Ibrahim Rauza
destinations.description: The twin tomb and mosque complex of Ibrahim Adil Shah II, often described as the finest building in Bijapur for its proportion and carving. It stands in a walled garden outside the old city.

destinations.name: Jumma Masjid, Bijapur
destinations.description: A large mosque begun by Ali Adil Shah I in the 16th century and left unfinished, with a vast prayer hall and a Quran written on its walls. It is still in use.
destinations.accessibility: Ground level with steps at the entrance

destinations.name: Malik-e-Maidan
destinations.description: A 16th-century cannon cast at Ahmednagar and brought to Bijapur, about 4 m long and one of the largest medieval cannons in the world, mounted on a tower. It is a short walk from the citadel area.

destinations.name: Bara Kaman
destinations.description: The unfinished mausoleum of Ali Adil Shah II, where the arches were planned to stand without a roof, giving the site its distinctive open silhouette. Only the base and a few arches were completed.

destinations.name: Asar Mahal
destinations.description: A hall built in 1646 to hold a hair from the Prophet's beard, with a facade of painted arches and a water tank in front. It later served as a court and a treasury.
destinations.hours: Daylight hours; entry restrictions may apply

destinations.name: Gulbarga Fort
destinations.description: A fort begun by the Bahmani sultan Alauddin Bahman Shah in the 14th century, with thick walls, 15 towers and the large Jama Masjid inside. It is a protected monument and the main heritage site of the city.

destinations.name: Khwaja Bande Nawaz Dargah
destinations.description: The dargah of the 14th-century Sufi saint Gesudaraz, a major pilgrimage site with a large mosque and an annual urs. The shrine is known for its Persian-influenced architecture.
destinations.season: Any season; urs draws large crowds
destinations.accessibility: Ground level; crowded during the urs

destinations.name: Sharana Basaveshwara Temple
destinations.description: A temple in the centre of Kalaburagi housing the samadhi of Sharana Basaveshwara, with a large tank in front and an annual jatra. It is an important Lingayat centre in the region.
destinations.accessibility: Steps at the tank and the shrine

destinations.name: Buddha Vihar, Kalaburagi
destinations.description: A large Buddhist temple and meditation centre built in the 1980s in the Ambekar-style vihara form, with a standing Buddha statue and a library. It is one of the largest viharas in Karnataka.

destinations.name: Sannati and Kanaganahalli
destinations.description: An archaeological site on the Bhima river where a Buddhist stupa with carved limestone panels and an Ashokan edict were excavated, now protected and partly displayed on site. Kanaganahalli is the find-spot of a portrait sculpture of Ashoka.
destinations.facilities: Site museum, none else on site

destinations.name: Amruteshwara Temple, Annigeri
destinations.description: A 12th-century Chalukyan temple with dense carvings on its outer walls and a stepped plan, often called the 'open air university of sculpture' by locals. It is a protected monument in Annigeri town.
destinations.facilities: None on site; town facilities nearby

destinations.name: Chandramouleshwara Temple, Unkal
destinations.description: A Chalukyan-era temple beside Unkal lake near Hubballi, with carved pillars and a small shrine, standing on a raised platform. It is a quiet protected monument away from the city centre.

destinations.name: Unkal Lake
destinations.description: A lake on the edge of Hubballi with a walking promenade, a garden and a statue of Swami Vivekananda. It is a popular evening spot and hosts a small boating facility.

destinations.name: Nrupatunga Betta
destinations.description: A low hill inside Hubballi with a park, a sunset point and a viewpoint over the city. It is a common walking spot for local residents.

destinations.name: Murugha Math, Dharwad
destinations.description: A Lingayat matha in Dharwad with a large campus, a temple and an educational institution, known for its social work. The matha is an active religious and cultural centre.

destinations.name: Harihareshwara Temple, Harihar
destinations.description: A 12th-century Hoysala temple at Harihar with a rare combined form of Vishnu and Shiva, and a sanctum reached by a flight of steps. It is a protected monument on the banks of the Tungabhadra.

destinations.name: Santhebennur Chennagiri Fort and Tank
destinations.description: A 17th-century fort with a large stepped tank, a walled enclosure and a temple, built by a local chief near Chennagiri. The tank is the most striking surviving element.
destinations.accessibility: Steps around the tank; rough ground

destinations.name: Kondajji Lake
destinations.description: A lake and garden about 12 km from Davanagere with a boating facility and a wooded shore. It is a local picnic spot.

destinations.name: Kalleshwara Temple, Malebennur
destinations.description: A Kalyani Chalukyan temple in Malebennur with finely carved doorways and pillars, protected by the state archaeology department. It is one of the better preserved temples of the period in this district.

destinations.name: Chennakeshava Temple, Belur
destinations.description: A Hoysala masterpiece consecrated in 1117 by Vishnuvardhana, covered in narrative friezes, bracket figures and lathe-turned pillars. The temple is still in worship and is on India's UNESCO World Heritage list as part of the Hoysala ensembles.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (ASI monument; indicative demo price shown)
destinations.accessibility: Ground level; a few steps at the entrance

destinations.name: Hoysaleshwara Temple, Halebidu
destinations.description: The 12th-century Hoysala temple of Shiva, with two shrines and some of the most detailed stone carving in India, including friezes of elephants, horses and epics. It is part of the UNESCO-listed Hoysala ensembles.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (ASI monument; indicative demo price shown)

destinations.name: Shravanabelagola
destinations.description: A major Jain pilgrimage centre where the 57-ft monolithic statue of Bahubali stands on Vindhyagiri hill, reached by around 600 steps. The Mahamastakabhisheka head-anointing ceremony is held roughly every twelve years.
destinations.fee_note: Free entry; footwear and camera charges apply
destinations.facilities: Steps, footwear deposit, shops, restrooms at the base
destinations.accessibility: Around 600 rock-cut steps; not accessible for limited mobility

destinations.name: Manjarabad Fort
destinations.description: A star-shaped fort built in 1792 by Tipu Sultan on a hill near Sakleshpur, with eight pointed bastions and a view over the Western Ghats. The laterite walls are largely intact.
destinations.facilities: None on site; shops at the base

destinations.name: Rosary Church, Shettihalli
destinations.description: The ruined shell of a 19th-century French-built church that is submerged when the Hemavathi reservoir fills and reappears in the dry season. It has become a well-known photography site.
destinations.hours: Daylight hours; visible mainly in the dry season

destinations.name: Bisle Ghat
destinations.description: A forest ghat on the road between Sakleshpur and Kukke Subramanya, with a viewpoint over the Bisle reserve and the Giri and Kumara Parvatha peaks. The road passes through rainforest and is closed in heavy rain.
destinations.hours: Daylight hours; check road condition in the monsoon
destinations.accessibility: Ghat road; viewpoint reached by road

destinations.name: Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangapatna
destinations.description: A major Vaishnava temple on the island of Srirangapatna, dedicated to Ranganatha reclining on Adishesha, with a gopuram and a large temple tank. The town was Tipu Sultan's capital and the temple predates his rule.

destinations.name: Dariya Daulat Bagh
destinations.description: Tipu Sultan's summer palace at Srirangapatna, a teak-framed pavilion with painted walls depicting his campaigns, set in a formal garden. It now houses a museum of the period.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (ASI monument; indicative demo price shown)

destinations.name: Gumbaz, Srirangapatna
destinations.description: The mausoleum of Tipu Sultan and his father Hyder Ali, with a polished black granite dome and carved doors, standing in a walled garden. The interior is known for its acoustics.
destinations.accessibility: Ground level; steps at the plinth

destinations.name: Brindavan Gardens, KRS Dam
destinations.description: Terraced gardens below the Krishna Raja Sagara dam, laid out in the 1930s, with fountains, a musical fountain show in the evening and a boating pond. The gardens sit on the Mandya district side of the dam.
destinations.hours: Approx. 06:00-20:00; musical fountain in the evening
destinations.facilities: Musical fountain, boating, restaurants, restrooms, parking
destinations.accessibility: Terraced paths and steps; some ramps

destinations.name: Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple, Melukote
destinations.description: A hill temple at Melukote associated with the Sri Vaishnava saint Ramanujacharya, with a large tank and the Academy of Sanskrit Research nearby. The town is also known for its handmade textiles and sweets.

destinations.name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
destinations.description: A riverine sanctuary on the Kaveri with islets where painted storks, herons, spoonbills and cormorants nest, visited by boat. It is one of the most important bird breeding sites in Karnataka.
destinations.accessibility: Boat boarding by steps; paths partly paved

destinations.name: Shivanasamudra Falls
destinations.description: Twin falls on the Kaveri, Gaganachukki and Bharachukki, where the river drops into a gorge about 90 m deep. Gaganachukki is viewed from a park and Bharachukki from a separate road on the other bank.

destinations.name: Siddaganga Math
destinations.description: A major Lingayat matha in Tumakuru known for its free boarding school and its social service work, with a large temple and dining hall. It is one of the most visited religious institutions in the state.
destinations.facilities: Dining hall, guest rooms, restrooms, parking

destinations.name: Devarayanadurga
destinations.description: A hill and forest reserve about 15 km from Tumakuru with a temple, a fort site and viewpoints over the plains. The road climbs through reserved forest to the temple at the top.
destinations.accessibility: Road to the top; steps at the temple

destinations.name: Namada Chilume
destinations.description: A spring near Devarayanadurga where water is said to have risen from a mark made by Rama's foot, set in a small reserve with a deer park. The site is a short drive from the Devarayanadurga temple.

destinations.name: Madhugiri Fort
destinations.description: A hill fort built on a 3,930-ft granite monolith, the second largest in Asia, with walls, granaries and a temple at the summit reached by steep steps. It is a protected monument.
destinations.accessibility: Very steep stone steps; not suitable for limited mobility

destinations.name: Jayamangali Blackbuck Conservation Reserve
destinations.description: A small grassland reserve near Maidenahalli protecting a population of blackbuck and grassland birds. Visits are usually arranged with the forest department.

destinations.name: Chitradurga Fort
destinations.description: A massive hill fort built in stages from the 11th century by the Nayakas and Hyder Ali, with seven concentric walls, nineteen gateways, temples, granaries and a stepped water tank. Its rock-hewn passages and the Onake Obavva story make it one of Karnataka's best-known forts.
destinations.accessibility: Extensive steps and uneven rock; not accessible

destinations.name: Chandravalli
destinations.description: An archaeological site with rock-cut caves, a temple and excavated layers going back to the Satavahana period. It lies in a valley just outside Chitradurga town.

destinations.name: Vani Vilas Sagar Dam
destinations.description: A dam built in the early 20th century across the Vedavathi river, with a garden and views of the reservoir, about 20 km from Chitradurga. It was among the earliest major dams in the region.

destinations.name: Aadumalleshwara Temple
destinations.description: A cave temple near Chitradurga town with a spring and a shrine to Malleshwara, set among rocks below the fort. The site is also a small picnic spot.

destinations.name: Kolaramma Temple
destinations.description: A Chola-era temple in Kolar town with inscriptions from the 11th century and a shrine to Kolaramma, the town deity. The temple's stone carvings and inscriptions are its main interest.
destinations.facilities: None on site; town facilities nearby

destinations.name: Someshwara Temple, Kolar
destinations.description: A Vijayanagara-period temple with a large gopuram, carved pillars and a mandapa, dedicated to Shiva. It stands close to Kolaramma temple in the old town.

destinations.name: Antaragange
destinations.description: A hill shrine near Kolar where water flows from a rock in the shape of a cow's mouth, with steps cut into the hill and a view over the town. It is a popular local pilgrimage site.

destinations.name: Avani Ramalingeshwara Temple
destinations.description: A group of temples at Avani in Mulbagal taluk, with Ramalingeshwara as the main shrine, known for its carvings and its association with the Ramayana. The site is also a centre of the Valmiki tradition.

destinations.name: Kolar Gold Fields (KGF)
destinations.description: The old gold-mining town of Kolar Gold Fields, with colonial-era mining infrastructure, churches and bungalows, where underground mining ran for over a century before closing in 2001. Visits are to the town's heritage buildings rather than the closed mines.
destinations.accessibility: Town roads; some sites closed to visitors

destinations.name: Kurudumale Ganesha Temple
destinations.description: A temple near Mulbagal with a large monolithic Ganesha idol, said to be one of the biggest in the region, and a Chola-period origin story. The shrine is a short detour from the Kolar-Mulbagal road.

destinations.name: Nandi Hills
destinations.description: A hill fortress retreat at about 1,480 m used by Tipu Sultan as a summer residence, famous for sunrise views above the clouds and for its cool climate. The road to the top is opened early in the morning, and entry is limited to a fixed number of vehicles.
destinations.facilities: Viewpoints, restaurants, restrooms, parking, Tipu's Drop
destinations.accessibility: Road to the top; steps at the viewpoints

destinations.name: Bhoganandishwara Temple, Nandi
destinations.description: A large temple complex at the foot of Nandi Hills built between the 9th and 11th centuries, with three shrines and a tank, among the finest early Chalukyan and Rashtrakuta work in the region. It is a protected monument.

destinations.name: Skandagiri (Kalavara Durga)
destinations.description: A 1,350-m hill near Chikkaballapura with the ruins of a fort at the top, trekked at night to reach the summit for sunrise. Entry is through a forest permit and a limited number of trekkers per day.
destinations.hours: Night trek; permits issued online in advance
destinations.facilities: Guide required, permit check at the base
destinations.accessibility: Steep trek of about 3-4 hours; not accessible

destinations.name: Gudibande Fort
destinations.description: A hill fort near Gudibande town with stone ramparts, a temple and rock-cut water tanks, built in the 17th century. The climb takes about an hour from the road.

destinations.name: Kaivara Kailasagiri
destinations.description: A temple site at Kaivara associated with the saint Narayanappa (Amaranarayana), with caves and shrines on a rocky hill. The site holds an annual fair that draws pilgrims from across the region.

destinations.name: Ramadevara Betta
destinations.description: The rocky hill near Ramanagara where the Hindi film Sholay was shot, with a temple, a cave and granite domes overlooking the town. It is a popular short trek and picnic spot.
destinations.accessibility: Steps to the temple; rough rock beyond

destinations.name: Janapada Loka
destinations.description: A folk-culture museum on the Bengaluru-Mysuru highway with reconstructed village houses, agricultural tools, puppets, masks and a regular folk performance programme. It was set up by the Karnataka Janapada Parishat.
destinations.facilities: Museum galleries, amphitheatre, restaurant, restrooms, parking

destinations.name: Mekedatu
destinations.description: A narrow gorge where the Arkavathi river cuts through granite, reached by a forest road and a short walk from Sangama. The name refers to a goat's leap across the channel.
destinations.fee_note: Free entry; forest vehicle fee may apply
destinations.accessibility: Rough forest road and steps; not accessible

destinations.name: Sangama
destinations.description: The confluence of the Arkavathi and Kaveri rivers near Kanakapura, with bathing ghats and a riverside walk. It is the starting point for the walk to Mekedatu.

destinations.name: Chunchi Falls
destinations.description: A waterfall on the Arkavathi downstream of Sangama, reached by a walk from the road through scrub and rock. The falls are best seen soon after the monsoon.
destinations.accessibility: Rough walk and rocks; not accessible

destinations.name: Savandurga
destinations.description: One of the largest monolith hills in Asia, about 1,226 m, with a fort at the base and a steep climb to the summit temple. The rock face is also used by rock climbers.
destinations.facilities: Temple at the base, small shops
destinations.accessibility: Steep rock climb with chains; not suitable for limited mobility

destinations.name: Himavad Gopalaswamy Betta
destinations.description: A hill temple at about 1,450 m inside Bandipur, dedicated to Krishna as Gopalaswamy, reached by a forest road. The hill is often wrapped in mist and is the highest point in the Bandipur area.
destinations.fee_note: Free entry; forest gate timings apply
destinations.accessibility: Road to the temple; steps at the shrine

destinations.name: Bandipur National Park
destinations.description: A tiger reserve on the Mysuru-Ooty road, part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, with dry deciduous forest and good chances of seeing elephants, gaur and deer on a safari. Safaris run from the park gate in the morning and evening.
destinations.season: October to March; park partly closed in the monsoon
destinations.facilities: Jeep safari, interpretation centre, restrooms, parking
destinations.accessibility: Safari jeeps; not accessible for wheelchairs

destinations.name: Biligiri Ranganatha Temple, BR Hills
destinations.description: A hill temple at about 1,700 m in the Biligirirangan Hills, sacred to the Soliga community and the centre of an annual festival. The surrounding hills are a tiger reserve and wildlife sanctuary.

destinations.name: Male Mahadeshwara Hills (MM Hills)
destinations.description: A major pilgrimage centre in the Eastern Ghats with a temple to Male Mahadeshwara and a large temple tank, drawing lakhs of devotees at its annual jatre. The hill sits inside a reserved forest area.
destinations.season: Any season; the jatre draws huge crowds
destinations.facilities: Guest houses, dining halls, restrooms, parking
destinations.accessibility: Steps and slopes; some ramps near the temple

destinations.name: Chamarajeshwara Temple
destinations.description: The main temple of Chamarajanagara town, built in the 19th century in the Dravidian style with a tall gopuram and a large tank. The town and district are named after the Wodeyar ruler Chamaraja Wodeyar.

destinations.name: Suvarnavathi Dam and Reservoir
destinations.description: A reservoir on the Suvarnavathi river near Punajanur with a garden and views of the BR Hills, popular as a picnic stop. The catchment lies inside the wildlife sanctuary area.

destinations.name: Badami Cave Temples
destinations.description: Four rock-cut cave temples of the 6th and 7th centuries, cut into a red sandstone cliff above a tank, with carvings of Shiva, Vishnu and Jain tirthankaras. They are among the earliest surviving examples of Badami Chalukyan art.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (ASI monument; indicative demo price shown)
destinations.facilities: Guides, steps to the caves, restrooms, parking
destinations.accessibility: Steps cut in rock; not accessible for limited mobility

destinations.name: Pattadakal Group of Monuments
destinations.description: A UNESCO World Heritage site with a group of 8th-century Chalukyan temples, including the Virupaksha and Mallikarjuna temples, showing early experiments in Dravidian temple form. The site sits on the banks of the Malaprabha.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (ASI monument; indicative demo price shown)
destinations.accessibility: Paved paths between temples; some steps

destinations.name: Aihole Group of Temples
destinations.description: A complex of over a hundred early Chalukyan temples of the 6th century, including the Durga temple with its apsidal plan and the Lad Khan temple, often described as a laboratory of Indian temple architecture. It is a protected ASI site.

destinations.name: Mahakuta Group of Temples
destinations.description: An early Chalukyan temple complex with a spring-fed tank and shrines to Shiva, about 14 km from Badami. The site is quieter than Badami and Pattadakal and still in worship.

destinations.name: Banashankari Temple, Badami
destinations.description: A temple to Banashankari near Badami with a large temple tank and a deepastambha, rebuilt in the 18th century on an older site. Its annual fair draws pilgrims from across north Karnataka.
destinations.accessibility: Steps at the tank and shrine

destinations.name: Bhutanatha Temple Group, Badami
destinations.description: A group of temples on the edge of the Badami tank, the largest in a stepped Chalukyan style and partly submerged in the monsoon. The setting at sunset is the draw.

destinations.name: Lakkundi Brahma Jinalaya
destinations.description: A 11th-century Jain temple at Lakkundi built under the Western Chalukyas, with a stepped plan, carved pillars and a museum of sculptures beside it. Lakkundi itself holds dozens of early temples and stepwells.

destinations.name: Kasivisvesvara Temple, Lakkundi
destinations.description: A finely carved Western Chalukyan temple at Lakkundi with dense relief work on its walls and pillars, protected by the ASI. It is one of the best preserved temples of the Kalyani Chalukya period.
destinations.facilities: None on site; Lakkundi museum nearby

destinations.name: Trikuteshwara Temple, Gadag
destinations.description: A temple in Gadag with three shrines to Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshwara on a single platform, and a Saraswati shrine with carved pillars. It dates to the Kalyani Chalukya period.

destinations.name: Veeranarayana Temple, Gadag
destinations.description: A Chalukyan temple in Gadag town with a large mandapa and shrines to Veeranarayana, still in worship and linked to the poet Kumaravyasa. It is a well-known local landmark.

destinations.name: Doddabasappa Temple, Dambal
destinations.description: A 12th-century Western Chalukyan temple at Dambal with a star-shaped plan and a dome of carved lotuses, protected by the ASI. The village also has a Jain temple of the same period.

destinations.name: Tarakeshwara Temple, Hangal
destinations.description: A large Western Chalukyan temple at Hangal with a hollow stepped tower and richly carved pillars and ceilings, protected by the ASI. Hangal was an important early capital in the region.
destinations.facilities: None on site; town facilities nearby

destinations.name: Kaginele Kanaka Guru Peetha
destinations.description: A matha at Kaginele, birthplace of the saint Kanakadasa, with a large temple, an art gallery and a research centre on the Haridasa tradition. It is an important centre for the Kuruba community.
destinations.facilities: Guest rooms, dining hall, restrooms, parking

destinations.name: Bankapura Nagareshwara Temple and Mosque
destinations.description: A Chalukyan temple and an adjoining mosque inside the old Bankapura fort, where the temple's pillars were reused in the mosque. The site is a protected monument.

destinations.name: Ranebennur Blackbuck Sanctuary
destinations.description: A sanctuary of open grassland and acacia scrub protecting blackbuck, wolves and grassland birds, spread over about 119 sq km. Visits are by forest road with permission.
destinations.facilities: Forest rest house, no visitor facilities

destinations.name: Galaganatha Temple, Hangal
destinations.description: A small Chalukyan temple near Hangal with a carved doorway and a stepped tower, standing in fields outside the town. It is a protected monument.

destinations.name: Anegundi
destinations.description: An old town on the north bank of the Tungabhadra said to be the original Kishkindha of the Ramayana, with a fort, temples and the Pampa Sarovar nearby. It is a quieter alternative base to Hampi.
destinations.accessibility: Rough streets and steps; not accessible

destinations.name: Koppal Fort
destinations.description: A hill fort with extensive stone ramparts, gateways and a stepped tank, held in turn by the Chalukyas, Bahmanis and Hyder Ali. It is a protected monument above Koppal town.

destinations.name: Kanakagiri Jain Temples
destinations.description: A group of Jain temples on a hill at Kanakagiri, an important Digambara pilgrimage site with a large idol of Parshwanatha and inscriptions. The site is busy during Mahavir Jayanti.

destinations.name: Gavimath, Koppal
destinations.description: A rock-cut cave associated with the saint Pampa, with inscriptions and a small shrine, near Koppal town. It is a protected monument of the early Chalukyan period.

destinations.name: Pampa Sarovar
destinations.description: A lake near Anegundi associated with the Ramayana and with the saint Pampa, with a temple on its bank. It is part of the Hampi-Anegundi heritage landscape.

destinations.name: Raichur Fort
destinations.description: A hill fort with a long history going back to the Kakatiyas and Bahmanis, with massive walls, gateways and a mosque inside. It is a protected monument above Raichur town.
destinations.season: None on site; town facilities nearby

destinations.name: Mudgal Fort
destinations.description: A fort at Mudgal with walls, bastions and a stepped tank, associated with the Bahmani and Vijayanagara struggles for the Raichur doab. It is a protected monument in Lingsugur taluk.

destinations.name: Maski (Ashokan Edict Site)
destinations.description: The site where an Ashokan minor rock edict was discovered in 1915, the first to name the emperor Ashoka, with a prehistoric ash-mound and megalithic burials nearby. The edict rock is protected and a copy is displayed.

destinations.name: Hatti Gold Mines
destinations.description: One of the oldest working gold mines in the world, with mining at Hatti recorded from ancient times and modern operations run by a state undertaking. Public access to the mines is restricted; visits are to the surface area and the town.
destinations.accessibility: Industrial site; access by permission only

destinations.name: Naradagadde Temple
destinations.description: A riverside shrine on the Krishna near Raichur with a temple and bathing ghats, visited during the annual fair. The site is a short drive from the city.

destinations.name: Yadgir Fort
destinations.description: A hill fort with stone ramparts, gateways and a large stepped tank, associated with the Bahmani and Adil Shahi periods. It is a protected monument overlooking Yadgir town.

destinations.name: Surapura Fort and Temples
destinations.description: A fort town on the Krishna with old temples, a palace site and a river ghat, once the capital of a local chieftaincy. The Sharanabasaveshwara temple and the fort walls are the main remains.

destinations.name: Chaya Bhagavathi Temple, Gogi
destinations.description: A village temple near Gogi known for its annual fair, when a large procession and cattle market are held. The shrine sits beside the Bhima river.

destinations.name: Hunasagi and the Bhima Valley
destinations.description: A taluk town on the Bhima with rocky river scenery, old temples and the nearby Yedhalli and Vibhuti falls country. It is a quiet base for exploring the district's prehistoric and temple sites.

destinations.name: Virupaksha Temple, Hampi
destinations.description: The principal living temple of Hampi, with a 52-m gateway tower and continuous worship since the Vijayanagara period, standing beside the Tungabhadra. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Hampi.
destinations.fee_note: Free entry; Hampi site ticket covers the monuments
destinations.facilities: Guides, restrooms, parking, shops along the bazaar street
destinations.accessibility: Ground level in parts; steps at the gopuram

destinations.name: Vittala Temple, Hampi
destinations.description: The most elaborate monument at Hampi, with the stone chariot in its courtyard and the musical pillars of the maha mandapa. It was built in the 16th century under Krishnadevaraya and is a UNESCO World Heritage monument.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (ASI monument; indicative demo price shown)

destinations.name: Lotus Mahal and Zenana Enclosure
destinations.description: A two-storeyed pavilion with lobed arches and a plastered facade in the royal enclosure at Hampi, once used by the royal women. The enclosure also holds the elephant stables and the watchtower nearby.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (ASI monument; indicative demo price shown)

destinations.name: Hazara Rama Temple
destinations.description: A compact Vijayanagara temple in the royal centre of Hampi, with Ramayana panels carved on its walls and a polished stone courtyard. It was likely the private chapel of the royal family.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (ASI monument; indicative demo price shown)

destinations.name: Queen's Bath, Hampi
destinations.description: An ornate 16th-century bathhouse in the royal enclosure, with a sunken pool surrounded by arcaded corridors and projecting balconies. It is one of the most photographed structures at Hampi.
destinations.fee_note: Ticketed (ASI monument; indicative demo price shown)
destinations.accessibility: Steps down to the pool level

destinations.name: Tungabhadra Dam and Garden, Hosapete
destinations.description: A large dam across the Tungabhadra near Hosapete with terraced gardens, a musical fountain and a viewpoint over the reservoir. It is the main irrigation source for the Ballari and Koppal districts.
destinations.fee_note: Free entry; garden and fountain ticketed on some days

destinations.name: Bidar Fort
destinations.description: A large Bahmani fort with triple walls, gateways, a citadel, a royal bath and a mosque, largely intact and protected by the ASI. The fort encloses palaces, gardens and water systems of the 15th and 16th centuries.
destinations.accessibility: Rough ground with steps; partly accessible by vehicle

destinations.name: Bahmani Tombs, Ashtur
destinations.description: A group of domed tombs of the Bahmani sultans at Ashtur, about 3 km from Bidar, with painted interiors and carved stonework. The tombs stand in open ground outside the city.
destinations.facilities: Rough ground; steps at the plinths

destinations.name: Madrasa Mahmud Gawan
destinations.description: A 15th-century madrasa built by the Bahmani prime minister Mahmud Gawan, with a minaret, a library and a facade of glazed tiles. It is a protected monument in the old city.

destinations.name: Guru Nanak Jhira Sahib
destinations.description: A Sikh gurdwara in Bidar associated with a visit by Guru Nanak, known for a spring whose water is said to have appeared at his word. It is a major pilgrimage stop in the Deccan.
destinations.accessibility: Ground level; ramps in the main areas

destinations.name: Narasimha Jhira Cave Temple
destinations.description: A cave temple near Bidar reached by wading through a spring-fed channel cut into the rock, ending at a shrine to Narasimha. The passage is short but wet and dark.
destinations.accessibility: Cave passage with water; not suitable for limited mobility

destinations.name: Basavakalyan Fort
destinations.description: A fort at Basavakalyan, capital of the Western Chalukyas and later a centre of the Lingayat movement, with walls, gateways and a mosque inside. The site is a protected monument.

experiences.name: Yakshagana performance evening
experiences.description: A demonstration booking for a two-hour Yakshagana performance with a short introduction to the costume and the tala system. Demonstration experience listing.

experiences.name: Coffee estate walk and cupping
experiences.description: Walk through a working coffee estate and learn how beans are picked, pulped and dried, ending with a tasting session. Demonstration experience listing.

experiences.name: Hoysala temple carving walk
experiences.description: A guided walk through the Hoysala temples at Belur and Halebidu, focused on the narrative friezes and the soapstone technique. Demonstration experience listing.

experiences.name: Coracle ride and Hampi bazaar walk
experiences.description: A coracle crossing on the Tungabhadra followed by a walk through the old bazaar street and the riverside ghats. Demonstration experience listing.

experiences.name: Bidriware craft demonstration
experiences.description: Watch the Bidri metal inlay craft being made and try a basic engraving under supervision. Demonstration experience listing.

experiences.name: Ilkal and Molakalmuru weaving visit
experiences.description: A visit to a handloom unit to see Ilkal sarees being woven on pit looms. Demonstration experience listing.

experiences.name: Udupi cooking session
experiences.description: A home kitchen session on Udupi cuisine, including sambar, rasam and a typical thali. Demonstration experience listing.

experiences.name: Kambala and coastal sport talk
experiences.description: An illustrated talk on Kambala buffalo racing and coastal sporting traditions. Demonstration experience listing.

experiences.name: Sandalwood carving workshop
experiences.description: A short workshop on sandalwood and rosewood inlay work with a local artisan. Demonstration experience listing.

experiences.name: Bird walk at Ranganathittu
experiences.description: An early morning guided bird walk along the Kaveri islets, with binoculars provided. Demonstration experience listing.

experiences.name: Badami cave art study walk
experiences.description: A slow walk through the Badami caves looking at Chalukyan sculpture and painting. Demonstration experience listing.

experiences.name: Coastal fishing harbour visit
experiences.description: An early morning visit to a fishing harbour with an explanation of the boats and the catch. Demonstration experience listing.
